clue.text: Mum's aria CD possibly featuring opera?

indicators.note: possibly says these letters could be arranged some other way, so they are to be reworked

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter

explanation.surface: A mother's recording of an aria might include a whole opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MUMSARIACD; 'featuring' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Music drama is Wagner's term for an opera in which music and text are fused.

clue.text: What ship's officer, without hesitation, will identify!

definitions.text: What ship's officer, without hesitation, will identify!

indicators.note: without tells us the officer's title loses the sound of hesitation

parts.note: a master is the captain of a merchant ship
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A ship's officer will point something out without a moment's pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes ER from MASTER. The whole clue also defines: a ship's officer would know a mast at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A mast is the tall spar on a ship that any officer aboard would recognise instantly.

clue.text: Wind indicator showing a sharp blow?

definitions.meaning: a windsock, the fabric tube at airfields showing wind direction

explanation.definitionFit: A windsock shows the wind, and a sock is also slang for a hard punch.

clue.text: Privileged and assured student, first-rate, on the way up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the pieces are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate, standing for a student

explanation.surface: A self-assured top student is rising fast with privileges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' reads the student and first-rate pieces upwards. Privileged here is the legal sense of communications kept secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Privileged information is secret, shared only with those entitled to it.

clue.text: One among the others took exam again

indicators.note: among puts one piece inside the other

explanation.surface: One student among the rest had to retake the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' places A inside REST.
explanation.definitionFit: To resit is to sit an examination a second time; resat is its past tense.

clue.text: Alternative to poison? Doctor's to employ some, on reflection

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

indicators.note: a reflection shows things backwards, so the word for some is turned round

explanation.surface: A doctor suggests a different way to deal with vermin after thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns the word for some round. A mousetrap is the poison-free way to deal with mice.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring trap is the usual way of killing rodents other than putting down bait laced with toxin.

clue.text: Edges of steam offering obstruction to vision

indicators.note: edges are a word's first and last letters, taken here from each of the two words

explanation.surface: Wisps of steam rising and blocking one's view.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'steam' and 'offering' give SM and OG.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick polluted fog blocks how far one can see.

clue.text: Kept shaking inanimate head of drunk?

indicators.note: shaking jumbles the word's letters into a new order
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A drunk kept shaking a head that seemed lifeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking' rearranges INANIMATE; 'head of' adds D from 'drunk'.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something in good order is to look after it, the sense of maintained.

clue.text: US bridge with unconventional dogleg neat

indicators.note: unconventional says the letters are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A bridge in America with an oddly neat dogleg bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unconventional' rearranges DOGLEG NEAT; 'with' is a link. A dogleg is a sharp bend, a golf term.
explanation.definitionFit: The Golden Gate is the famous suspension bridge at San Francisco.

clue.text: Another drunk collars you finally — prepare to fight!

indicators.note: to collar is to grab round the neck, so one piece wraps round the other
finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A second drunk grabs someone, ready for a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collars' wraps the drunk round the last letter of 'you'; 'finally' picks that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxing referees call this phrase to clear the ring as a round is about to start.

clue.text: What doctor may prescribe for an irritant?

explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a common prescription, and a tedious person is informally called this.

clue.text: "Beer sold out", for example, upset part of college

indicators.note: out says the letters are disordered
upset in a down clue turns the piece upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A notice reading beer sold out upsets part of the college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SOLD into SLOD; 'upset' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge colleges the gatekeeper's office by the entrance bears this name.

clue.text: Drink to excess? That's to strike nerve

definitions.meaning: to drink heavily, to take to alcohol
read literally: hit means strike and bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to start drinking heavily; read word by word it says to hit courage, as bottle means nerve in British slang.

clue.text: Very keen on melon in picture looking good for the camera

indicators.note: in places the pair of pieces inside the other word
in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: the Ogen is a variety of melon

explanation.surface: Someone keen on melon in a photo that turns out flattering.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ogen is an Israeli melon variety, little known outside Britain; 'on' stacks the pieces in a down clue and 'in' puts them inside the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who photographs well always looks attractive in pictures.

clue.text: Mark flower coming up -it's sweet and fragile

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue reads the word from the bottom, backwards

explanation.surface: A mark on a flower as it rises, sweet and fragile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reads the flower from the bottom of the down light. A brandy snap is a British biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin crisp rolled ginger biscuit, often filled with cream, that breaks easily.

clue.text: Farm machine revs and earth will go all over the place

indicators.text: will go all over the place
indicators.note: going all over the place means the letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: A tractor revving as earth flies everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will go all over the place' rearranges REVS EARTH; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A combine is the machine that gathers in crops at the end of the season.

clue.text: Poor quality -but at a fraction of the usual cost?

definitions.text: at a fraction of the usual cost?
definitions.meaning: read literally, a rate one third of normal

explanation.definitionFit: Inferior goods are called this, and read literally it is a price one third of the usual.

clue.text: Rather weak government leads to mild concern

parts.note: thin means rather weak, as of soup

explanation.surface: Feeble government gives rise to some unease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a thing about something is to have a slight obsession or worry over it.

clue.text: It's believed to show limitations to the linking of computers

indicators.note: limitations are boundaries, so the first and last letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A doctrine shows the limits of computer networking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limitations to' gives TE, the first and last letters of 'the'; 'to show' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle or doctrine is something held to be true.

clue.text: One military policeman standing up, admitting force is not ideal

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: admitting lets the piece in, so it goes inside the other

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A military policeman standing to attention lets in a force that is not ideal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' lets force inside. 'Standing up' looks like a reversal sign for the policeman, but it is a synonym in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flawed falls short of perfection.

clue.text: Cords accompanying puppets in musical production

parts.note: guys are ropes or cords holding a tent or mast steady
dolls are like puppets, toy figures

explanation.surface: Strings and puppets in a staged musical show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Broadway musical by Frank Loesser, set among New York gamblers.

clue.text: Head on and on, going round island

indicators.note: going round says the pair of words wrap about another piece

explanation.surface: Head on and on, circling an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts I between the two ONs.
explanation.definitionFit: Onion is British slang for the head, as in off one's onion, meaning mad.

clue.text: Some amethyst or carnelian necklace

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A necklace made with some amethyst or carnelian gemstones.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is a metal neck ring worn by ancient Celts.

clue.text: Fairy nearly in danger

indicators.note: nearly means the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A fairy is almost in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the last letter of PERIL; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a sprite in Persian mythology.

clue.text: Muses, showing a little canniness

indicators.note: a little says only a short run of letters inside the word is used

explanation.surface: Muses showing a touch of shrewdness.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'canNINEss'; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: There were nine Muses, so the number names the group, the Nine.

clue.text: Italian friend embracing daughter,18?

indicators.note: embracing means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: an Italian friend is a pal in Rome, read as a phrase

explanation.surface: An Italian friend hugging a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian friend' becomes PAL IN ROME, and 'embracing' puts D inside. 18 is TENET, which reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The word at 18 across spells the same backwards and forwards, the example being given in place of the definition.

clue.text: Carbon-copy cloak

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a sleeveless outer garment hanging from the shoulders.

clue.text: One Catholic to pull up left-winger backing the latest thing in France

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the whole sequence is read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
RC is short for Roman Catholic
to rein in a horse is to pull it up
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A Catholic stops a left-wing activist who backs the newest French fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the whole string of four pieces round; 'to' is a link. The answer is French, used in English too.
explanation.definitionFit: French for the last cry, it means the newest fashion.
